newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state sells 26.5 pct of joint bank.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state sells 26.5 pct of joint bank.

text.p: The Egyptian state has sold off 26.47 percent of joint venture Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank as part of its privatisation programme, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said on Monday.
The CMA said in a statement the state had sold 300,000 shares at 301 pounds each, which is about 15-fold what it had offered investors last week.
The state-owned National Investment Bank said investors could bid for 20,400 shares, which represents 1.8 percent of the total 1.125 million shares, at any price from a minimum 140 pounds ($41.2).

Alexandria Commercial and Martime shares are rarely traded and are denominated in U.S. dollars and Egyptian pounds. The bank said new shareholders would be entitled to a 1996 dividend which has yet to be decided by the bank's board.
State owned firms and banks own a large tranche of Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank. The shareholders include the Bank of Alexandria, Misr Insurance and Public Holding for Shipping.
The privatisation is in line with the goverment's programme to get out of joint-venture banks. The state is also considering privatising one of its major retail banks.
Published figures showed that Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank made unaudited net pre-tax profits of 35.4 million pounds in calendar 1996 compared to 16.8 million in the previous year.
The bank's assets rose to 1.09 billion in 1996 from 925.8 million in 1995. Customer deposits were also higher in 1996 at 790 million from 679.9 million in the previous year.
